label: early-middle copy steps (recall 2-4) of long sequences
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>), concentrated on recall positions 2-4 (t = 10-13) of long sequences (L = 8-9 hold ~87% of mass; nothing for L <= 4). Within that window it fires on only ~26% of steps; activation is boosted when x (and to a lesser degree l, s, f) is about to be output in the next 1-4 steps (next_out = x lift 6.5x), and top examples show it firing over the copy steps leading up to an x and switching off once x is output. Upcoming-token content alone explains under half the mass, so the token dependence is diffuse. Weak tail on the final copy steps of L=9. Dev F1 ~0.38, mass recall ~0.73.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: x, l, s, f, 0, z; least: 2, j, -, k) and the previous input (most: d, h, i, 0, 2, u; least: q, g, t, z); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, L=9, t=17.
